mil-bulk.label: City of Milwaukee bulky item pickup

mil-drop.label: City of Milwaukee Drop Off Centers

tasks.label: Load handled by a paid hauler

prep.label: Who the route is for
prep.text: The property must receive solid-waste collection from City of Milwaukee Sanitation Services. A Milwaukee mailing address alone leaves collection service unclear.

prep.label: Amount and request
prep.text: For eligible bulky items, the department describes up to 1 cubic yard at the regular collection point. Larger eligible loads need a special request and a fee. Check the current size and fee schedule before setting out a load.

prep.label: Proof of access
prep.text: The city describes access for its residents and property owners. It asks for government-issued photo ID and lists separate paperwork for owners who live outside the city.

prep.label: Load and vehicle
prep.text: Center staff set the assessed volume and may decline restricted vehicles or loads. Staff do not unload. Check the current payment and vehicle rules before traveling.

prep.label: Scheduling
prep.text: Contact Public Works for the fee and collection arrangement. Verify your service address under the city’s program before placing items at the curb.

prep.label: Fee basis
prep.text: The city distinguishes ordinary bulky items from appliances and TVs. Share the complete list when you ask for a quote, including any combination of those types.

prep.label: Proof of access
prep.text: The center requires a current Wauwatosa address on a valid Wisconsin driver’s license. Commercial and contractor vehicles are excluded.

prep.label: Load
prep.text: Sort items for their separate receptacles and check current hours, fees and payment methods on the city’s own page.

rules.text: The city lists furniture and mattresses as bulky items. Check whether the combined pile fits the regular limit or needs a special pickup.
The city excludes TVs from bulky pickup and directs them to a Drop Off Center.
The city excludes appliances from bulky pickup and directs them to a Drop Off Center.
The special bulky service excludes loose material and mixed loads containing items such as construction waste, recyclables, tires, brush or yard waste.
The published service applies to properties that receive city sanitation collection. Ask the city about your property and have the hauler identify its receiving facility separately.
The city lists old furniture and mattresses. Drop-off fees depend on the volume assessed by staff.
The drop-off page gives a per-TV fee and a limit of three. Confirm current charges and the eligible load with the city.
Appliances are on the city’s recycling list. Confirm your exact appliance and the receiving rules before loading.
The centers separate material streams and inspect loads. Read the accepted-item list and verify every unusual material and the vehicle before departure.
This city page describes a residential and property-owner program. It leaves the hired hauler’s access unclear. Ask the hauler to identify the receiving facility and confirm the terms.
The city lists sofas and mattresses as examples for a paid curbside pickup. The bulky fee is based on item count.
The city lists paid curbside pickup for TVs. The quoted amount depends on the pickup’s other items.
The city lists paid curbside pickup for refrigerators and other major household appliances, with a first-item and additional-item fee.
The published page gives individual item categories and examples. Ask Public Works about the entire mixed load and any items that need a different route.
Confirm whether the city will serve the address and what needs a separate hauler. Obtain a written scope from any contractor you separately hire.
The city lists bulky household furniture and mattresses. The posted refuse fee depends on the amount brought in.
The Drop Off Center page lists TVs at $30–$45 each. Special Collection describes a $30 drop-off charge in its appliances and TV section. Confirm your television’s charge directly.
The city lists refrigerators and other major appliances. The Drop Off Center page gives a separate per-appliance fee.
The city describes separate receptacles and asks visitors to keep the material categories apart. Check each item and the household-use limits before loading.
Wauwatosa limits this center to household use and explicitly excludes commercial and contractor vehicles.
